With independent HomePod volume on for an app, the HomePod slider sets its level on the speaker; it starts no higher than the app's current Windows volume, so the speaker never suddenly gets louder. Apps sent to "Both" can then be set separately on the speaker and this PC; apps sent to "HomePod" are already silent here, and their Windows volume no longer changes the speaker; apps sent to "This PC" aren't sent. Independent volume enables per-app routing, adding about {0} ms of latency to what is sent. Windows mute or zero volume also silences the speaker; while an app's audio sessions have different Windows volumes, or one is below 1%, the speaker temporarily plays at Windows volume × HomePod volume. Turn independent volume off to follow Windows again.
